name: rosetta-literals-string
code:
use IO.Std.write_line

let name = "world"

// Every string literal in ghul interpolates, so there is no separate quote
// that expands variables and none that suppresses it. There are no verbatim
// strings and no here-documents; adjacent literals chain instead, which is
// how a long one is written across several lines.

write_line("a plain string literal")
write_line("interpolated: hello, {name}")
write_line("escaped: a tab[\t], a quote[\"], a backslash[\\]")
write_line("braces are doubled: {{ and }}")
write_line("unicode by code point: \u20AC and \uD83D\uDE00")
write_line(
    "adjacent literals chain, "
    "so this is one string "
    "written over three lines")

let letter = 'g'

write_line("a character literal: {letter}")

write_line("escaped: a tab[\t], a quote[\"], a backslash[\\]")

write_line("unicode by code point: \u20AC and \uD83D\uDE00")
